id: Slowly but Surely: Twenty Years of Wayne Youle-The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington-Event Brite
name: Slowly but Surely: Twenty Years of Wayne Youle
venue: The Dowse Art MuseumLower Hutt, Wellington
long_description:
Overview
A talk on Wayne Youle and his place in New Zealand art, given by Auckland Art Gallery's Nathan Pōhio.
The Dowse Art Museum invites audiences to a special floor talk with Nathan Pōhio on Sunday 16 August at 11am. Pōhio is Kaitiaki Matua, Toi Māori | Senior Curator, Māori Art at Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki.
In this illuminating discussion, Pōhio will situate Wayne Youle's practice within the broader landscape of New Zealand and Māori art. Pōhio will reflect on the humility, wit, conceptual rigour, themes and community engagement that define Youle’s art making to date, drawing on more than 20 years of watching him thrive as both an artist and a respected member of the Ōtautahi arts community.
The talk coincides with Wayne Youle: Back In Five, a major survey exhibition charting two decades of Youle’s practice.
Read less

id: Requirements Elicitation-Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Requirements Elicitation
venue: Venue To be Confirmed | Wellington CBDWellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview



Gain a core understanding of requirements elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques.
Description
This one-day course provides a core understanding of elicitation, the importance of planning, and coverage of many valuable elicitation techniques. Emphasis is also placed on the need to verify requirements with the business to confirm that an accurate understanding has been elicited. During the afternoon session course participants undertake a realistic elicitation exercise, to reinforce the principles and techniques learnt during the course.
Greater emphasis is being placed on skilled business analysts who have the ability to communicate strongly, engage with stakeholders, and elicit a clear understanding of business requirements. Requirements elicitation skills have never been more important for business analysts and IT professionals.

The Requirements Elicitation course is delivered by seasoned Equinox consultant practitioners who apply the techniques and practices presented in this course on a daily basis.

Outline
Introduction to Requirements Elicitation
Goals of elicitation
Elicitation in the analysis process
Requirements elicitation methodology
Plan
The need for planning
Common elicitation problems
Requirements elicitation techniques
Requirements election patterns
Selection criteria
The requirements elicitation plan
Do
Preparing for the elicitation session
Performing elicitation
Managing the elicitation session
Presenting the elicitation results
Check
Communicate the requirements set
Check elicitation results
Check elicitation process
Act – corrective action
Requirements elicitation exercise

Learning outcomes
Following the completion of this course, students will be able to:
Identify where requirements elicitation fits within the broader requirements process
Understand and adopt an elicitation methodology
Select appropriate elicitation techniques for the situation
Plan and manage a requirements elicitation session
Understand the need for verification of elicitation results

Audience
The primary audience for this course is business analysts and systems analysts of all levels of experience. The course will also be of value to any project team members who are involved in elicitation or requirements activities.

Prerequisites
It is recommended that participants have some experience with requirements in project environment before attending.

id: Finding Tiny Moments of Joy in Everyday Life-Project 100Nelson, Nelson Region-Event Brite
name: Finding Tiny Moments of Joy in Everyday Life
long_description:
Overview





Do you need more joy and calmness in your life? Then this workshop about how to find small joys in the world might be for you!
In an increasingly frenetic world with social media and news cycles encouraging us to see things as increasingly doom and gloom, this workshop will help you recalibrate by using micro journaling to rediscover the small joys in your everyday life.
Because while we can’t change the big things, sometimes a small shift to a more positive outlook can help us go about our day-to-day lives less stressed and more resilient.
With fun, practical steps George Penney, author of the US, UK and Australian bestselling book of people watching vignettes, Tiny Moments of Joy: Spotted on Market Day in Aotearoa New Zealand, will guide you through looking at the world around you with fresh eyes, finding moments of peace, calm and even happiness.


For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

id: Info Session on Family Law-Kapiti Women's CentreParaparaumu, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Info Session on Family Law
long_description:
Overview
This practical information session is designed to guide you through the key steps following a separation.
Doors Open: 10.15am
Info Session on Family Law
Hosted by the Craft Your Life Wisdom Circle, KAPITI
The session covers what to do immediately after separating, when and how to address relationship property, and the right time to engage a lawyer.
You will gain clarity on separation agreements, your legal entitlements, and what life looks like after signing.The session also explains mediation, the process if an agreement cannot be reached, and potential court proceedings.
Ideal for those seeking clear, structured guidance to make informed, confident decisions during a challenging transition.
Join us for the Craft Your Life Wisdom Circle in KAPITI, a group designed for people seeking connection, encouragement, fresh perspective, and practical wisdom as they grow into their next season with confidence and purpose.
Brooke Young, solicitor, has a natural passion for connecting with people. She believes that the best outcomes are achieved through realistic advice and a focus on keeping clients informed and empowered throughout the legal process.
Her key areas of interest span family law — including Parenting Orders, Protection Orders, relationship property and separation matters — as well as trusts work covering establishment, administration and wind-ups.

id: INSPIRE Festival-Nayland CollegeNelson, Nelson Region-Event Brite
name: INSPIRE Festival
long_description:
Overview


INSPIRE Festival is for all tamariki aged 8-13 (up to year 8) who are interested in STEAMS learning.
Public ticket sales open on 7 August. Early access is currently available by invitation only.

INSPIRE Festival is 4-5 Sept 2026!
$60 per child per day for a full day of STEAMS learning!
INSPIRE Festival 2026 offers two days of student selected challenging discussions and hands-on workshops all focused around STEAMS (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Maths, and Society). This year the festival is being hosted at Nayland College!
• Friday: 1- or 2-hour workshops
• Saturday: 2-4 hour, in-depth workshops. Perfect for students to get really stuck in to topics.
INSPIRE offers thought-provoking discussions and hands on experiments for AGES 8-13 (up to Year 8). Students choose up to 4 sessions to attend, all based on the STEAMS model of education and delivered by New Zealand's top professionals, scientists, businessmen, and mentored college students.
INSPIRE will develop the connection between classroom theory and some very exciting and ground-breaking real careers which make a difference in our world. The inaugural INSPIRE was in 2012 and massive demand has led to it being hosted annually with over 650 students attending and has continued to grow. The energy and enthusiasm of the students is wonderful and, with their feedback, demonstrates the necessity and benefits of INSPIRE. All attendees will be our future leaders and creative thinkers and they have told us they want more; more challenge, more connections and more opportunities to grow and learn.
It is recommended that students attending INSPIRE Festival have a teacher/adult 'in-charge' of them. Students left at the venue without an adult 'in-charge' are left at their own risk.
Programme Description and TIMETABLE:
https://heyzine.com/flip-book/79774ff44c.html

id: Physical Oceanography Workshop 2026-Earth Sciences New Zealand - WellingtonWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Physical Oceanography Workshop 2026
venue: Earth Sciences New Zealand - WellingtonWellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview












The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.




Welcome to the biannual New Zealand Physical Oceanography Workshop (POW).
As climate change fundamentally reshapes our marine environments, understanding the fluid dynamics, heat distribution, and structural dynamics of our oceans has never been more critical. This year, our community gathers under a vital, unifying theme: The physics of the ocean in the age of multiple stressors.

We invite abstracts and presentations exploring the fundamental physical processes driving—and reacting to—global environmental change:
Coastal Oceanography of New Zealand
High-Latitude and Polar Dynamics
Next-Generation Ocean Modelling & Data Integration
Cross-Disciplinary Climate Solutions
How to do oceanography in the age of gestures broadly

Call for Abstracts & Registration Details
Oral Presentations: Standard 15-minute slots (including Q&A).
Lightning Talks: Project snapshots—ideal for introducing preliminary findings, novel scripts, or new field deployments.
How to Submit: Please email your presentation title, authors' list, a brief abstract (max 250 words), and your presentation preference directly to the organising committee at oceanography.newzealand@gmail.com.
Abstract Submission Deadline: 20 August 2026
Registration Deadline: 20 August 2026
Hybrid Registration Deadline: 1 September 2026
Registration is $100 for general attendees and free for students. We also have a free hybrid attendance option with the ability to present. Early-career researchers are highly encouraged to present.

We are planning a fun dinner on Wednesday, and we aim to finish early on Thursday.
We're looking forward to seeing you in September!

id: Men's Circle & Breathwork-Bhakti Lounge WellingtonWellington, Wellington-Event Brite
name: Men's Circle & Breathwork
long_description:
Overview
A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, breathwork and meaningful connection in a space of trust and support.
Men's Circle & Breathwork 
Starts at 6pm
In a world where men are often expected to have everything figured out, this gathering offers a space to be genuine, not perfect.
This is a free event, with an optional plant-based dinner available for $15. While there’s no obligation to stay for dinner, sharing a meal together offers a meaningful way to strengthen connections.
Andre and Sri Jiva co-host this circle with a shared passion for creating authentic, supportive spaces where men can connect deeply, offering this gathering simply because they believe in its importance.
The Men’s Circle provides a safe and nurturing environment where men can share openly, express their feelings and encourage personal growth. Through honest sharing and collective support, participants build resilience, deepen self-awareness, and strengthen their sense of identity and purpose.
 Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
Breathwork is a powerful practice to help ground the nervous system and connect to a deep presence. 
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
 Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.
Join us after this free event for an optional plant-based dinner and dessert for only $20 (or $10 for students).
Meet Andre, your host:
Andre has been immersed in men’s work since the age of 13, when he first experienced a rite of passage in Golden Bay. That formative experience sparked a lifelong connection to circle work, which he later deepened by returning as a mentor. A multi-instrumental musician, poet, and pranayama (breathwork) facilitator, Andre also brings his passion for ecstatic dance, philosophy, and authentic connection into his offerings. He is deeply inspired by the question of what it means to be human, how we can more fully experience our aliveness, our depth, and reconnecting with the beauty of life together.
Meet Sri Jiva, your host:
Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

long_description:
Overview
The people, politics and ideas that shaped New Zealand’s conservation legacy, hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
As New Zealand debates proposed changes to our conservation laws, there has never been a better time to hear from two people who played a pivotal role in shaping our conservation history.
Join former Prime Minister and former Conservation Minister, the Rt. Hon. Helen Clark, and former Minister of Conservation and former Nelson mayor, Hon. Philip Woollaston, for a special lunchtime conversation exploring the people, politics and ideas that shaped modern conservation in New Zealand.
Helen and Philip were New Zealand’s second and third Conservation Ministers, respectively.
Drawing on their first-hand experience, they will reflect on the vision, challenges and decisions behind some of New Zealand's most significant conservation legislation and discuss the legacy it continues to leave today.
The conversation will be facilitated by Johny O'Donnell and hosted by West Coast-Tasman Labour candidate, Rory Paterson.
Bring your lunch, bring your curiosity, and enjoy an engaging discussion, with plenty of time for audience questions.
Admission is free. Koha at the door is appreciated.
We’ll also have raffles and a silent auction, so bring some cash if you’d like to support our West Coast-Tasman campaign.
Seating reservations on a first-come, first-served basis.

long_description:
Overview






A workshop that will take you through the A to Z of writing a character driven romance novel from bestselling author George Penney.
Do you have dreams of typing “The End” on a romance novel you’ve written but don’t know where to start?
Have you always dreamed of being a writer but find the actual process of becoming one intimidating?
Or maybe you’re a forever-writer just looking for pointers for how to shape your ideas into a structure that’ll sell to readers.
This three hour workshop will take you from initial character creation, through romance story structure and then to practical tips on getting your romance novel finished.
You’ll be taken through different romance genres, how to come up with three-dimensional, interesting characters, how to built tension and conflict, tips on writing good sex scenes and how to write that truly satisfying Happy Ever After ending.
This is a practical workshop designed to leave attendees motivated, excited and equipped with the tools to go on and finish that book!

*Please note: This is an AI free writing workshop. We believe that writing should be a messy, wonderful, exasperating, rewarding process that explores the depth of human creativity rather than a test on how well someone can type a prompt into a LLM. If you'd like to argue this point, please send us a non-AI hardbound treatise of no less than one hundred thousand words, hand-written in iambic pentameter.

For all other Beautiful Words events, go to www.beautifulwords.net

id: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON-AJ ParkWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: 2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON
long_description:
Overview
"The Future of IP Dispute Resolution" by Sir Colin Birss, Chancellor of the High Court of England and Wales
5.30pm | Pre-event refreshments
6.00pm | Public lecture

The Future of IP Dispute Resolution
The legal landscape is changing before our eyes. The advent of AI and digital assets, the internationalisation of dispute resolution, and the changing expectations of users, all pose challenges, and intellectual property has always raised issues of its own.
This lecture will examine the state of intellectual property litigation today in the wider context, consider where it needs to be in future, and look at how we need to adapt to meet the challenges.
The topics include the major legal problems in IP which will need to be addressed; the legal and practical impact of artificial intelligence; the importance of digital assets and tokenisation; and the emergence of alternative modes of resolving dispute resolution.
Colin Birss is the Chancellor (Head of the Chancery Division) of the High Court of England and Wales. Called to the English Bar in 1990, he practised intellectual property law. In 2010 he became judge at the Patents County Court (now IPEC), in 2013 he went to the High Court, and in 2021 to the Court of Appeal. He was Deputy Head of Civil Justice 2021-25, and appointed Chancellor in 2025. He sits in the Court of Appeal and in the High Court.

If you are a University of Melbourne alumni, information about your participation may be shared with the Advancement team, as explained in our privacy notice.

id: Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?-Russell McVeaghWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?
long_description:
Overview
A global perspective on investment, reliability, and the risks of getting it wrong.
Three recent shocks to electricity markets - cheap renewables, declining storage costs, and the return of demand growth - have led some to conclude that electricity markets as we know them have run their course. Drawing on thirty years of restructured markets abroad, this presentation will argue that these developments actually strengthen the case for markets — and will explore what reliability means, and how it should be provided, in a greener electricity system.
Professor James Bushnell – Biography
Professor James Bushnell is a distinguished scholar whose research and policy contributions have helped shape modern understanding of electricity markets, energy regulation, and climate policy, making him one of the most influential voices in energy economics. He is an internationally recognised expert in energy economics, electricity markets, environmental policy, and industrial organisation.The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of Russell McVeagh
Date and Time: Thursday 3 September, 4pm - 6pm @Russell McVeagh, 157 Lambton Quay, please join us for a drink and nibbles from 4pm, presentation to start at 4:30pm with a Q&A to follow.
Please email admin@erganz.org.nz with any dietary requirements.
RSVP: Registrations can be secured by clicking on "Reserve a Spot".

id: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry-HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry
venue: HMLT002 Hugh Mackenzie BuildingWellington, Wellington Region
long_description:
Overview
Why are semiconductors central to global power? This keynote explores state-market tensions, supply chains, and geopolitical rivalry.
Using the global semiconductor industry as a case study, this lecture explores ‘decoupling’ amidst the complex web of state-market relations.
Most studies of decoupling focus on the United States and China. In contrast, I focus on the relationship between the United States and the full range of key semiconductor producers (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China). I ask when, and how, states intervene in semiconductor markets and propose that while the main actors in the semiconductor supply chain are not hegemonic powers, their high production capacities mean that their power is ‘pivotal’.
I argue that while technology production chains reflect the conflicting interests of states, because production chains also embody key shared interests, states cannot completely ‘decouple’ from one another. Meanwhile, key stakeholders are not always states, but also private companies and skilled workers. These actors have their own interests as well, meaning that production chains become further intertwined, rendering true decoupling impossible. Their resistance to decoupling means that this ‘stickiness’ will be a feature of any state-led attempt to forge supply chain independence.

id: Capital Connection: An hour with the Prime Minister-Banquet Hall, New Zealand Parliament BuildingsWellington, Wellington-Event Brite
name: Capital Connection: An hour with the Prime Minister
venue: Banquet Hall, New Zealand Parliament BuildingsWellington, Wellington
long_description:
Overview


Wellington Chamber of Commerce and Pax8 are proud to host the Prime Minister, Christopher Luxon.
Join Business Central and the Wellington Chamber of Commerce for an exclusive breakfast event featuring Prime Minister Rt Hon Christopher Luxon in conversation with Hayley Horan, Chief Executive of Business Central.
Set within the iconic Banquet Hall at Parliament, this special event offers members and the wider business community a rare opportunity to hear directly from New Zealand's leader in a professionally moderated fireside chat.
Unlike a traditional keynote speech, this event has been designed as a genuine conversation. The discussion will be informed by the experiences, perspectives, and questions submitted by Business Central and Wellington Chamber members, helping to ensure the topics explored reflect the realities, opportunities, and challenges facing our business community today.
Designed to be engaging, insightful, and business-focused, the discussion will explore the opportunities and challenges shaping New Zealand's future. From economic growth, productivity, trade, infrastructure, workforce development and artificial intelligence, through to geopolitics and New Zealand's long-term competitiveness, the conversation will focus on the issues that matter most to businesses across our region.
Following the fireside chat, attendees will have the opportunity to participate in a live audience Q&A, providing further engagement with the Prime Minister and valuable insight into the Government's priorities and vision for New Zealand.
Your Ticket Includes:
Shared breakfast at a round table with fellow business leaders
Exclusive access to a one-hour conversation with the Prime Minister
Opportunity to submit questions that may shape the discussion
Live audience Q&A
Networking with business, government, and community leaders before and after the event
Agenda:
7.00 am - Guest arrival & networking
7.20 am - Guests seated for breakfast buffet
7.45 am - Prime Minister to speak
8.05 am - Q&A with audience
8.30 am - Closing formalities

Why Attend?
Whether you're a business owner, executive, manager, entrepreneur, policy professional, or emerging leader, this event offers a rare opportunity to gain direct insight into the issues shaping New Zealand's future while connecting with some of the region's most engaged and influential business people.
Bring your questions. Share your perspective. Help shape the conversation.
Spaces are limited and demand is expected to be high. Register early to secure your place and ensure your voice is part of the discussion.

id: Just A Drink Speed Dating (Age Range Mid-20s – Mid-30s)-Waitoa Victoria StWellington, Wellington Region-Event Brite
name: Just A Drink Speed Dating (Age Range Mid-20s – Mid-30s)
long_description:
Overview








Apps are shit. This is less shit. Everyone comes with a single friend they think is worth meeting. 6-10 dates. ~5 mins each. Drink included.

Just A Drink Speed Dating
We put on events so that the single people worth meeting can meet each other without having to open an app.

How This Event Works
This event works by asking everyone to come in pairs. We do this for two key reasons:
You’ve both got someone to go with. Good company is guaranteed and moral support is built-in.
If someone has been brought along by a friend, they’re probably all good. We love that everyone at our events is someone another person there can vouch for.

What We're Trying To Help With
It's hard for the single people worth meeting to find each other.
Out and about, you can’t always tell who’s single.
The apps have helped – you’ve probably met some good people through them – but it can still be hard to tell who’s actually worth leaving the house for.
So, here’s another way to meet people.
Come along. It’s just a drink.
